name: Critical minerals
summary: China extended its pause on new rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027; April 2025 licensing still in force
state: China's commerce ministry extended its suspension of new export controls on rare earths and related items to 10 Jan 2027, alongside a two-month tariff pause, as the US–China truce was due to lapse on 10 Nov (The National, 9 Nov; SMM). The extension is short and earlier licensing requirements for seven rare earths remain, so Watch holds. Trump and Xi are expected to meet at APEC in Shenzhen in the week of 16 Nov; no stoppages outside China linked to bans were found as of 12 Nov.
for_you: Manufacturers of magnets, electric vehicles, electronics and defence equipment are exposed to licensing delays for Chinese rare earths.
rubric_hit: Watch: Chinese rare-earth licensing still in force; no export bans causing stoppages outside China (Alert line)

sources.title: The National — China extends pause on rare earth export curbs for two months
Shanghai Metals Market — China extends suspension of rare earth export controls until January 2027

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
